verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is in wire copy, and the finding's own source is the wire copy: the Zacks piece syndicated on Yahoo on 2026-09-01 states the $2.68 EPS consensus 'has remained unchanged over the past 60 days' and the $297.8M revenue figure, one day before the print. The Q1 surprise magnitudes are also published verbatim — Investing.com's 2026-06-04 transcript headline is literally 'Argan's Q1 2027 earnings surpass forecasts with 78% EPS surprise', which is the $3.24 vs $1.82 in this finding. The FY27 $1.28B / $12.09 aggregate is a public consensus screen. What is genuinely un-drawn is only the bridge (annual implies ~$330M/~$2.95 per quarter vs a Q2 stub of $297.8M/$2.68), and that bridge mixes a Zacks quarterly consensus with a 5-analyst annual from a different aggregator, which is exactly how unrevised quarterly splits behave on a lumpy EPC name. Two further problems: the premise that Q2 is 'Argan's seasonally strongest construction quarter' is wrong — FY26 went Q1 $193.7M, Q2 $237.7M, Q3 $251.2M, so Q3 is the seasonal peak and a modest Q1-to-Q2 step is not anomalous. And the mechanism is directly falsified by this name's own most recent reaction: on 2026-06-04 Argan beat by 78% on EPS and 16.7% on revenue and the stock moved +0.77%. A 15.7% option-implied move also says nobody is treating $2.68 as a tight anchor.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Zacks consensus of $2.68 EPS unchanged for 60 days and $297.8M revenue, plus the Q1 beat of 42.7%/15.2% — the finding's own source, published the day before the print.
Headlines the 78% Q1 EPS surprise, i.e. the $3.24 vs $1.82 comparison this finding uses.
Q1 FY27 revenue $290.954M and diluted EPS $3.24, the sequential base for the arithmetic.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-06-04 print produced a +0.77% move on a 78% EPS surprise — the single most direct refutation available that a beat-versus-stale-consensus is what moves AGX. Front-expiry implied move of 15.7% with 47.6% realised vol shows the market is not anchored on the point estimate. Reaction history is dominated by backlog/order news, not EPS: -11.98% on 2025-12-04 despite a record $3.0B backlog headline, +37.91% on 2026-03-26.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published sell-side note in the last two weeks explicitly re-basing Q2 revenue toward $330M, or evidence that the $2.68 is a genuine 5-analyst mean rather than an unrevised aggregator stub, would drop this toward 45.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Short interest is a semi-monthly public exchange release, republished by every screen including the finding's own source, and Benzinga runs a standing 'Looking Into Argan's Recent Short Interest' series on this exact ticker. The level is not an outlier: Benzinga puts the AGX peer-group average at 6.27% of float against AGX's 6.5-7.4%, so this is a peer-typical position, and 3.28 days to cover on ~277k shares of average daily volume is trivially coverable — not squeeze fuel. The 65% year-over-year rise in days-to-cover is as much a volume-denominator artifact as a positioning statement. Most damaging, the claim's direction is undefined: the same fact is offered as informed bearish positioning and as squeeze kindling, and the baseline's own positioning read cuts against the bearish version — put/call open interest is 0.31, i.e. the listed book is call-heavy, and 25-delta put skew is only 2.63 vol points, a mild rather than an alarmed downside bid. This is the textbook 'structural and known' case: real, public, and not worth much either way against a 15.7% implied move.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The finding's own source — short interest, percent of float and days to cover, published on a free public screen.
Standing Benzinga coverage of AGX short interest, noting the peer-group average of 6.27% of float — i.e. AGX's level is in line with peers.
Short interest, borrow rate and short-squeeze metrics for AGX published continuously.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Put/call open interest ratio 0.31 on 8,200 total contracts and 25d put skew of only 2.63 vol points: the option market is paying modestly for downside, not pricing a crowded-short unwind or an informed short. Nothing in the 5-day (-8.43%) or 20-day (-33.22%) run-up isolates a short-driven move; the drawdown window maps onto dated news (see interactions).
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A borrow-rate spike or utilisation above ~90%, or short interest above ~15% of float, would make this a real positioning claim rather than a peer-typical statistic.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The headline balance is not a buried footnote — contract liabilities of $565.774M at 2026-04-30 versus $513.969M at 2026-01-31 appear in the 2026-06-04 earnings release exhibit itself, and the cash consequence was the release's second headline (total cash and investments $973.6M versus $895.0M, net liquidity $421.4M, no debt). The customer-funded working-capital structure of Gemma's large gas EPC contracts is the best-known single feature of the AGX story and the reason the company carries roughly a billion of cash; every bull note recites it. What is genuinely 10-Q-only and un-drawn anywhere I could find is the roll-forward decomposition — $222.6M recognised out of the opening balance, hence ~$274M of fresh advances — and the $36.9M contract-asset offset. So I credit real obscurity on the arithmetic and none on the fact. Against that: it is a Q1 datum, three months old, filed 2026-07-02, and it will be superseded within hours by the Q2 balance sheet. As a forward read it says Argan is billing ahead of cost on projects entering peak construction, which is the same thing the Q1 revenue beat already said and which the market answered with +0.77%.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q1 FY27 earnings release exhibit carries contract liabilities of $565.774M versus $513.969M and cash/investments of $973.6M versus $895.0M — the balance itself was in the release, not only the 10-Q.
The 10-Q (filed 2026-07-02, not 2026-06-04 as the finding states) contains the revenue-recognised-from-opening-balance disclosure the arithmetic rests on.
Wire coverage of the Q1 release leading on record revenue, margin and cash.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The tape gave the Q1 release, cash build included, +0.77%, and then fell 7.3% four weeks later on the backlog/insider read — the market has demonstrated it is not paying for AGX's working-capital float. No option-chain feature keys on this.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the Q2 print shows contract liabilities falling while revenue accelerates, the advance-funding read reverses and the Q1 decomposition becomes the setup for a genuine surprise; I would drop this to 30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I verified the absence-of-filings claim directly and it is factually correct — EDGAR shows only five 8-Ks in 2026 (2026-03-26 item 2.02, 2026-04-08 items 8.01/9.01, 2026-06-04 item 2.02, 2026-06-10 items 5.07/8.01, 2026-08-04 items 8.01/9.01 = the $8.3M ValCor teledata bolt-on), so no power-EPC award has been announced since 2026-04-08, and no award press release exists in the window either. The backlog series is also correct ($3.0B at 2025-10-31, $2.929B at 2026-01-31, $2.767B at 2026-04-30 — the finding's '2026-10-31' is a typo for 2025-10-31). But every one of those points was a press-release headline, and the decline plus its interpretation has been published and traded: Quiver ran 'Argan Falls as Investors Weigh Insider Selling and a Small Backlog Pullback' on 2026-07-02 on a day the stock fell 7.3%, quoting 'near-term order momentum' concerns; Zacks has since written that 'backlog declined from $2.93 billion to $2.77 billion as existing projects progressed faster than new awards were announced'; and the ratings followed — Zacks Research cut to Hold on 2026-08-07, Weiss to B- on 2026-08-11, Wall Street Zen to Hold mid-August. Meanwhile the tape is -33.22% over 20 days and -48.35% from the 52-week high. There is also a logical hole the finding concedes against itself: Q1 added roughly $125M of backlog with no 8-K at all, so zero award 8-Ks is weak evidence of zero bookings, and the third-consecutive-decline number depends on a Q2 revenue figure the finding gets from the bullish sibling claim. I still rate this the least-priced of the six: the specific arithmetic landing at $2.4-2.7B is unpublished, and backlog is demonstrably the variable this stock trades on.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Attributes a 7.3% single-day fall to insider selling plus the $2.9B-to-$2.8B backlog pullback and 'questions about sustaining the project pipeline'.
Company press-release headline states backlog of $2.8B versus approximately $2.9B at 2026-01-31 — the decline was the headline.
Establishes the $3.0B peak at 2025-10-31 in a press-release headline.
Publishes the 'handful of new projects over the next 10 to 18 months' guidance and the $2.8B/79%-gas backlog composition.
Zacks piece on the drawdown noting backlog fell from $2.93B to $2.77B because existing projects progressed faster than new awards were announced.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The -33.22% 20-day move begins around 2026-08-04 and spans the downgrades of 2026-08-07 through mid-August, so order-momentum concern is visibly in the price. Against that, backlog is what has historically produced the large reactions on this name (-11.98% on 2025-12-04, +37.91% on 2026-03-26), and the 15.7% implied move is consistent with a market that expects a backlog shock in either direction — which is why I size this large even while rating most of the narrative published.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If Argan announces an award concurrently with the print, or discloses Q2 additions above ~$400M, the third-decline premise fails outright; conversely a sell-side note in the last week already forecasting sub-$2.5B backlog would push this above 85.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both legs and the supposed twist are all in mainstream wire copy, and the twist has been in headlines. The Abbott directive was covered on the day by the Texas Tribune (the finding's own source), Houston Public Media and Utility Dive, then by Forbes on 2026-08-06 and again on 2026-08-12 under 'Data Center Moratoriums And The Rise Of Private Grids', and by client alerts from Gibson Dunn, Holland & Knight and Troutman Pepper Locke — all of which state that the audit does not reach behind-the-meter projects that do not intend to connect to ERCOT, naming Fermi and Pacifico's on-site gas-turbine projects. Bisnow's headline was 'Texas Pauses Data Center Power Connections, Which Could Speed Up Rapid Development'. On the Pennsylvania side, Utility Dive's headline on the Shapiro order was literally 'Pennsylvania dangles permitting carrot for data centers that bring their own power', syndicated further. So the exemption for on-site generation is not an obscure detail a hunter surfaced; it is the framing several outlets chose. The only unpublished step is naming Argan as the beneficiary, and even that is the oldest part of the AGX bull case. Price evidence is strong: the 20-day window over which the stock lost 33.22% starts right at the 2026-08-03 Abbott order, so the market has already traded this policy set — including whatever offset it believes the exemption provides. Mechanism also only reaches the print through call commentary, not through any reported Q2 number.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The finding's own source: Abbott freezes new Texas data-center interconnections pending a PUCT/ERCOT audit.
Client alert setting out the directive's scope, including that it does not reach behind-the-meter loads not connecting to ERCOT.
Headlines that Pennsylvania's order offers a permitting carrot to data centers that bring their own power — the same offset the finding claims is undrawn.
Argues the Texas pause may accelerate development because on-site-generation projects are exempt.
Frames data-center moratoriums as driving a shift toward private, behind-the-meter generation.
Shapiro executive order sharply restricting Pennsylvania data-center permitting.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: -33.22% over the 20 trading days beginning approximately 2026-08-04, i.e. the window opens the day after the Abbott order and contains the 2026-08-18 Pennsylvania order; the 2026-08-29 Yahoo piece describes the fall as a sector-wide reassessment of power-project exposure. That is the price having moved on exactly this news. Realised vol of 47.6% against 103.3% ATM IV says the market is still paying for policy tail risk.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the audit is shown to sweep in ERCOT-connected projects that Gemma is already building — i.e. the exemption does not in fact cover Argan's Texas backlog — the sign flips and the claim becomes materially unpriced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This was in the wire copy the day the Form 4 hit. MarketBeat published 'Insider Selling: Argan (NYSE:AGX) Director Sells $3,313,222.24 in Stock' on 2026-08-04 carrying the exact 5,716 shares, the $579.64 average, the 2,533 remaining direct shares and the 69.29% reduction figure this finding reports; StockTitan carries the filing page as well. Insider selling at AGX is also a months-old, thoroughly published theme rather than a new datum: Quiver on 2026-07-02 documented 31 insider trades over six months, all sales, zero purchases, roughly $108M disposed, including the non-executive chairman's 30,000 and 20,000 share sales in June, on a day the stock fell 7.3%; Sahm Capital wrote up an independent director selling 28% of their holding back on 2026-04-07. The 69% figure is also overstated as a statement about ownership: I read the Form 4 and it discloses 8,000 shares held indirectly in 'John R. Jeffrey, IRA', so total beneficial holding went from 16,249 to 10,533, a 35% reduction, not 69%. And the size is immaterial — $3.3M by one non-employee director against a roughly $5.8B market capitalisation, preceded by a Form 144 filed 2026-07-31, which is the signature of a pre-announced routine sale rather than a signal. The 'executed within 4% of the 52-week high' observation is true of essentially every insider sale that happens near a top and carries no information about the print.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Reports the 5,716-share sale at $579.64, the $3,313,222.24 proceeds, 2,533 shares remaining direct and the 69.29% reduction — the same day the Form 4 was filed.
31 insider trades in six months, all sales, ~$108M, including the chairman's June sales, on a 7.3% down day.
The Form 4 itself: open-market sale, code S, 2,533 direct shares remaining plus 8,000 held indirectly in an IRA the finding omits.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The -33.22% 20-day window begins around 2026-08-04, the exact date this Form 4 and its MarketBeat write-up landed, so whatever the sale was worth is inside the realised move rather than ahead of it. A Form 144 was filed 2026-07-31 pre-announcing the sale, so the market had notice before the trade printed.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A cluster of sales by the CEO or CFO dated inside the closed window before this print, unreported by the aggregators, would be a different claim and I would rate it near 20.

interactions: Three overlaps matter. (1) AGX-1#0 and AGX-1#3 are mirror readings of the same two documents — the 2026-06-04 release and the Q1 10-Q — and they are not independent: #3 needs $320-350M of Q2 revenue to force backlog down to $2.6-2.7B, which is precisely the beat #0 argues is coming. A large revenue beat mechanically accelerates the backlog burn-down, so #0 being right makes #3 more right, and both cannot be scored as separate edges without double counting the same quarter. (2) AGX-1#2 is the cash-side reflection of #3's revenue-side claim, drawn from the same 10-Q: customer advances rise as the same projects that are draining backlog enter peak billing. Rising contract liabilities alongside falling backlog is one phenomenon described twice, not two findings. (3) AGX-1#3, #4 and #5 all compete for the same realised price move. The 20-day drawdown of -33.22% begins on or about 2026-08-04, which is the day the Form 4 and its MarketBeat write-up hit and the day after the Abbott order, and the window contains the 2026-08-07/08-11/mid-August ratings downgrades and the 2026-08-18 Pennsylvania order. That one move cannot be evidence that three separate things are still unpriced. Separately, one factual correction that does not change my numbers: #3's 'RUPO of $3.0B at 2026-10-31' is a typo for 2025-10-31, and #2's source_date of 2026-06-04 is the earnings date, not the 10-Q filing date, which was 2026-07-02.
